punchline: On Rosling's three-answer quiz about the world, people did worse than a chimpanzee guessing at random, and their mistakes all leaned gloomy.
thirty_sec: Hans Rosling asked people simple multiple-choice questions about the world. With three answers each, a chimp guessing would get a third right. Only about 13 percent knew that 80 percent of the world's one-year-olds are vaccinated, and about 7 percent knew extreme poverty had almost halved. The wrong answers all leaned toward the gloomier option. He wrote about it in Factfulness.
